title: Flavor serialization_format default is resolved at call time, not hard-coded in the signature
answers: models logged on Databricks switched serializer, cloudpickle default lost
why does sklearn log_model default to skops here but cloudpickle on Databricks
serialization_format default changed after upgrade on Databricks runtime
pytorch log_model pickle vs pt2 default depends on environment
body:
Symptom: On Databricks Runtime or with a databricks tracking URI, a model logged without serialization_format is saved as skops (sklearn/LightGBM) or pt2 (PyTorch) instead of the cloudpickle/pickle that earlier releases wrote, changing artifacts and dependencies.
Root cause: the save_model/log_model signatures in mlflow/sklearn/__init__.py, mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py and mlflow/lightgbm/__init__.py hard-coded the non-Databricks default value.
Fix pattern: default the parameter to None and, when it is None, resolve it inside save_model and log_model via the flavor's _get_default_serialization_format, which checks is_in_databricks_runtime() or is_databricks_uri(mlflow.get_tracking_uri()).
Constraints: Only applies when the argument is omitted; explicit values override. PyTorch export_model=True resolves to pt2 before the Databricks check and must stay that way.
applies: Any MLflow flavor whose save/log API has a serialization_format parameter with environment-dependent defaults.
says: Models logged in the Databricks environment unexpectedly changed their saved artifact format.
Saved machine learning models on Databricks no longer use the previous default serialization format.
Logging a model without choosing a format generates unexpected dependencies in the workspace.
Keep the traditional serializer as the default when saving models on Databricks clusters.
Model artifacts logged to a Databricks tracking server changed format after our platform upgrade.
search: Default serialization formats for model flavor save and log APIs must be resolved dynamically at call time rather than hard-coded in function signatures. In mlflow/sklearn/__init__.py, mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py, and mlflow/lightgbm/__init__.py, save_model and log_model default serialization_format to None and resolve it via _get_default_serialization_format using is_in_databricks_runtime() or is_databricks_uri(mlflow.get_tracking_uri()). Omission of this check causes unconfigured models on Databricks to save as skops or pt2 instead of cloudpickle or pickle. Explicit serialization_format arguments override the default, and PyTorch export_model=True resolves to pt2 prior to the Databricks environment check.
